### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via validateSecurityPosture (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via validateSecurityPosture (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7ffc57846a97afde24fbfc59b6b05d7562ef4df0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a68927550841c9abbd9e2dd98e427847ddcf98ab` — the merge of head `d72dd96391abac31819a19979a55186ad472e7cc` into base `7ffc57846a97afde24fbfc59b6b05d7562ef4df0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a68927550841c9abbd9e2dd98e427847ddcf98ab && git checkout a68927550841c9abbd9e2dd98e427847ddcf98ab
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7ffc57846a97afde24fbfc59b6b05d7562ef4df0 d72dd96391abac31819a19979a55186ad472e7cc && git checkout -B drift-repro 7ffc57846a97afde24fbfc59b6b05d7562ef4df0 && git merge --no-ff d72dd96391abac31819a19979a55186ad472e7cc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7ffc57846a97afde24fbfc59b6b05d7562ef4df0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7ffc57846a97afde24fbfc59b6b05d7562ef4df0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8e4f65c2c69c384290be528f8503e5bbc91f977c`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23549 (body; comments `6180310991` triage, `6180412113` claim, `6181479521` os-dev-report), PR #23560 (body, file list, the API diff, which equals `git diff origin/main...branch` byte-for-byte modulo index lines: 4 files, +385/-13, merge-base `086fa4640`), the check-runs on the head, and committed source on `origin/main` (`7ffc57846`) and the branch. Tier basis: by the PR's file list neither the path arm (`packages/spec/src/**`) nor the declaration arm (`Clause-②: yes`) hits and no governed path is touched; the review was asked at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` by the claim for the save door's accept-set narrowing, and that is the tier served, as the brief fixed it. Note for the posting seat: `record-recognisers.mjs` `reviewFace()` over this PR's four paths answers the `declaration` face (`TIER_DEFAULT`, no schema and no governed path), and `servedTierStands()` is exact in either direction; a reader that derives the face from the file list will not read a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` line as standing on this PR, so the seat should post the tier its reader expects (the judgments below do not change with that line).

Check-runs on `8e4f65c2c`, as found at read time (not waited on): 38 runs. completed/success (23): Auto Label, Build Core, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · source gates, filter. completed/skipped (6): Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix), Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Temporal Conformance. in_progress (9): Test Core 1/6 through 6/6, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · workspace. `Check Changeset` green is the verdict of `check:empty-changeset`, `check:adr-0087-registration` and `check:changeset-no-major` on this head (pr-automation.yml steps 897-898, 976-977, 1127). The all-green landing condition is the seat's to apply once the nine conclude.

### ① Derived judgments

(a) The narrowing, judged RIGHT in the code. `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts` :772-:799 (unqualified-key loop) now reads `dot = flsKey.indexOf('.')` and skips only a dot above position 0; :845-:851 (unknown-field loop) skips a dot at or below position 0. The two guards are disjoint and exhaustive over every key, so each key reaches exactly one loop and earns at most one finding; both shapes share the one pre-existing `findings.push` site and the file's push-site pin stays at 16 (test :1932, was :1873 on main, same value). Verdict per key, read off the guards and pinned by the new `it.each` table and the save-door pin:
- `'.FIELD'`, `'.'`, `'..x'`, `'.x.y'` (dot at 0): before, loop 1 skipped them for containing a `.` and loop 2 took skip 1 on the empty head (`flsGraph.has('')` is false); now loop 1 reports `security-fls-unqualified-key` at `error`, loop 2 skips. Exactly one finding each. RIGHT.
- bare key (no dot, index -1): loop 1 fires on its no-dot branch, loop 2 skips. Unchanged. RIGHT.
- `OBJECT.FIELD` real, `OBJECT.` and `OBJECT.a.b` on an in-stack object (dot above 0): loop 1 skips, loop 2 judges as before (empty or dangling remainder stays `security-fls-unknown-field`). Unchanged. RIGHT.
- `no_such_object.x`, `no_such_object.` (dot above 0, head not in `flsGraph`): loop 1 skips, loop 2 takes skip 1 as before. Unchanged. RIGHT; the card's "another package may declare it" reason still holds only for a non-empty head.
- The refusal is right in every deployment: `PermissionEvaluator.getFieldPermissions` (plugin-security `permission-evaluator.ts` :440-:441) keeps a key only when `key.startsWith(objectName + '.')` and `ObjectSchema.name` is `z.string().regex(/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/)` (`object.zod.ts` :2042), so the prefix is at least two characters and never begins with `.`; a key whose first character is `.` can match no registered object. `PermissionSetSchema.fields` stays `z.record(z.string(), ...)` (`permission.zod.ts` :888), untouched.
- Observation, out of the card's shape and byte-unchanged by this diff: the empty-string key `''` takes the bare-key branch and its pre-existing hint offers `'crm_opportunity.'`, a key the unknown-field rule refuses. Not introduced here; not a finding against this diff.

(b) The doors, judged against `origin/main` code. The lint table reaches the runtime only through `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` (protocol.ts :6913), called from `saveMetaItem` (:22714, state `active` unless `mode: 'draft'`) and `promoteDraftForPublish` (:24339, via `publishMetaItem` :23839). The second save-door gate `runAuthoringGate` (:6850) dispatches per-type plugin gates, not the lint table. `validateSecurityPosture` is in `AUTHORING_RULES` with `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME` and `runtimeTypes` including `permission` (`authoring-rules.ts` :2003-:2012). Door by door:
- publish-mode `saveMetaItem` and the draft promotion: gated. RIGHT, and both pinned on a real kernel.
- permission-set clone (`runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.ts` :348, no `mode`, so `'publish'` by `saveMetaItem`'s default :21940): gated. RIGHT.
- `duplicatePackage` (protocol.ts :26880, `mode: 'publish'`; the gate's own comment says it is deliberately NOT carved out): gated. RIGHT.
- `importUnmanagedPackage` (:27114, `mode: 'publish'`): gated. RIGHT.
- organization-ownership ceremony (`cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts` :572, no `mode`, no `source`): gated. RIGHT.
- `os migrate meta` re-save of a converted active row (`migrateStoredMetadata`, :23669): WRONG. That call passes `source: 'migrate-stored'`; `saveMetaItem` forwards it as `writeSource = request.source ?? 'protocol.saveMetaItem'` (:21858) into the gate, and `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` returns `[]` on `evt.source === 'migrate-stored'` (:7009) before any rule runs. The carve-out's comment names "the migration would report `failed` while leaving the body in the OLDER dialect" as exactly the outcome it exists to prevent. So the row is rewritten (`outcome: 'rewritten'`), the lint never judges it, and nothing is reported `failed`. The changeset (bullet "At the save door ...", clause "and `os migrate meta` when it re-saves a converted active row (that row is then reported `failed` and keeps reading as stored)"), the PR body ("Where it now refuses", same clause), and the ADR-0087 marker's sentence "A stored set holding such a key keeps loading until it is next saved, and that save is judged" all state a refusal that does not happen. This text ships to consumers as `CHANGELOG.md` for a security narrowing: an operator reading it would expect a migrate pass to surface stored `'.FIELD'` keys, and it will not. The same over-statement, smaller: "every door that saves through `saveMetaItem`" also covers the `package-author` authoring channel, which the gate exempts (:6993); the author-time CLI doors judge that channel's source instead.
- H4, judged RIGHT: `@objectstack/lint` is imported from `src` only by `packages/cli` and `packages/metadata-protocol`; in metadata-protocol the table runs only inside the two write verbs above; the CLI callers (`validate`, `lint`, `compile` for `os build`/`os dev`, `verify`, `scaffold-validate`, `author-time-rules`, `artifact-packages` for the build's per-package pass, `sdui-manifest`) judge source config at author time. No registry load, boot or read path runs the lint, so a stored set keeps loading until its next gated save; the draft save is ungated by D1 and pinned so.

(c) The texts, judged RIGHT. The no-dot (bare-key) message and hint are byte-identical to the pre-change strings (the diff moves them under a ternary and changes no character), as are `severity`, `rule`, `where` and `path`. The `dot === 0` message names the empty object part ("its object part (before the first '.') is empty, so the key matches no object, is silently IGNORED, and the declared masking never enforces."); the hint names the OBJECT.FIELD form (spelled with angle-bracket placeholders in the runtime text) and appends an example only when the remainder is non-empty and contains no `.`, so `'.'`, `'..x'` and `'.x.y'` get the form alone and `'.x'` gets `'crm_opportunity.x'`, a key the rules accept. Pinned by the third new unit case, which asserts the example absent for all three multi-dot or empty spellings.

File surface, judged in the claim's bounds: `.changeset/23549-fls-empty-object-part.md`; `validate-security-posture.ts` hunks at :754-:799 and :844-:886, both inside the two FLS loops and nothing else; its unit test; one save-door pin file in `packages/objectql/src`. Nothing under `packages/spec/**`, nothing in plugin-security, no other lint rule, `rule-explanations.ts` identical to main. No export line added or removed anywhere in the diff.

### ② Semver level

RIGHT on every declaration; the one wrong sentence is in the changeset's prose, judged under ① (b) and repaired there.
- Package and level: only `@objectstack/lint` changes published code (the lint unit test and the objectql test file do not publish). `minor` with a `**BREAKING** (an accept-set narrowing)` banner is the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs` header: breaking ships as `minor`, `major` refused) and AGENTS.md rule 3 (`(narrowing)` is BREAKING). No bump for `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is right: its code does not change. Matches the precedent `.changeset/pre/22042-nested-validation-predicate-verdict.md`, which bumped metadata-protocol only because its code moved.
- Clause-②: `no (narrowing)` in the claim, the PR body and the changeset. RIGHT: the diff widens no surface. `SECURITY_FLS_UNQUALIFIED_KEY` and `SECURITY_FLS_UNKNOWN_FIELD` are defined at the same lines on main and branch (:133-:134); the refusal rides the existing `INVALID_METADATA` 422; no export, signature, schema key or registry entry is added (the id string appears in 13 files on the branch vs 11 on main, the two new ones being this changeset and the new test). The lane charter's branch test (`lanes/spec.md` :35-:36: a consumer with no different branch to act on gets the existing member's message widened, not a new code) is met: the id, the runtime consequence and the remedy are the bare key's. A new rule id or error code would have made it `yes (narrowing)`; none is added.
- ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: RIGHT for this diff. No authorable key, export or stored shape moves, no row is converted, and no ledger entry could derive the repair (an empty object part does not say which object was meant). The alternative `registered` is impossible for that reason. The gate re-validates the category statement-against-statement and is green on this head (`Check Changeset`).
- The dev's deviation (before/now in words, no literal FROM → TO label): RIGHT. AGENTS.md rule 3 requires the FROM → TO mapping when the change removes or renames something an author can write; nothing authorable is removed or renamed here (`'.FIELD'` never enforced and never had a working spelling). `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` reads a FROM/TO label USED as a section label or table header as a migration prescription (branch 1 of its detector), which would contradict the disposition. The #22042 precedent carries the same "Remedy." paragraph shape and passed. Not a dispatch-text breach: the dispatch named no FROM → TO requirement.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none. Nothing to answer or escalate.
- Out-of-scope note (`security-fls-unqualified-key` has no `os explain` entry; carrier #22161, noted not filed): judged correctly handled. The diff makes no explain text false: the `security-fls-unknown-field` entry's "Not judged" list names the three graph skips, not the dot guard, and still holds for that rule, which now skips the empty head too. The claim allowed touching `rule-explanations.ts` only if its text names the guard; it does not, and #22161's census slices own the file serially. Pre-existing gap, polish; leaving it to the carrier is right. The seat may want #22161 to know the unqualified-key message now has two shapes with no entry.
- Deviation, merge of `origin/main` before opening (`086fa4640`, two commits: #23539 in metadata-protocol `protocol.ts`/`reference-sites.ts`, #23547 in spec tests): in policy, AGENTS.md Multi-agent 10 says pull `main` before opening a PR and scope the re-check to the overlap. Neither incoming commit touches lint or objectql; the save-door pin, the lint suite and all 65 derived gates were re-run on the final head, and the three full consumer suites at the pre-merge head cover the same diff. Not a file-surface matter; the merge commit carries git's default message. No action.
- Deviation, sixth pin case (draft save lands, its publish refused 422, only the draft row stored): in surface. The claim names "one save-door pin on a real kernel"; the case sits in that one file and pins the second gated door (`publishMetaItem`), the door the changeset names. Right to add.
- Deviation, two in-surface test edits: in surface ("its unit test"). `remainder` joins the receiver meta-test's PLUMBING set because the test scans the rule source for every `identifier.property` receiver and would otherwise report `remainder.length` / `remainder.includes` as an untabled schema read; a string local, exactly as `flsField` is listed. The skip-1 comment rewrite (and the matching source comment at :877-:886) removes a recorded disposition this card reverses; leaving it would record `'.description'` as deliberately unjudged while the rule above now judges it. Both necessary and bounded.
- Deviation, H4 measured with a temporary test file never committed: no surface impact; the committed pin covers the two gated doors, and the ungated-load claim is read off the importers and call sites above.
- Deviations on attribution trailers and the private fetch ref: process notes, outside the file surface and the contract; no action here.
- Required repair (the FAIL): one sentence, three places, no code change. In `.changeset/23549-fls-empty-object-part.md` remove the clause "and `os migrate meta` when it re-saves a converted active row (that row is then reported `failed` and keeps reading as stored)" from the save-door bullet, and state instead that `os migrate meta --stored --apply` re-saves are not judged (the gate exempts `source: 'migrate-stored'`, so a stored set holding such a key is rewritten into the current dialect unjudged and keeps loading); amend the ADR-0087 marker's "and that save is judged" to except that pass; optionally qualify "every door that saves through `saveMetaItem`" to publish-mode saves outside the `package-author` channel. Mirror the same clause in the PR body's "Where it now refuses" paragraph. The dev's H4 reading and the pins need no change.
